title: On the principal eigenvalue for compound Poisson processes

predicted_errors.error_location: Theorem 2.1 and its proof in Section 4
predicted_errors.supporting_evidence: The asserted formula λ_1^X(D)=r|D|^{-1}∫_D∫_{D^c}j(y-x)dydx is generally false. For a killed compound Poisson process the killed generator is r(K_D-I), where K_Df(x)=∫_D j(y-x)f(y)dy, so the principal decay rate is r(1-ρ(K_D)), with ρ(K_D) the spectral radius of K_D, not r times the spatially averaged one-step escape probability. These quantities agree only in exceptional cases where the constant function is a principal eigenfunction, e.g. when the one-step retention probability is constant on D.

The proof replaces the law of S_n conditioned on survival through every time 1,...,n with the law of S_n conditioned only on S_n∈D. Lemma 4.4 concerns the latter event, whereas Lemma 4.5 conditions on ∩_{k=1}^n{S_k∈D}. These are not equivalent. Survival conditioning weights paths by all preceding transitions and, in general, converges to a quasi-stationary distribution rather than the uniform distribution on D. Consequently the claimed limit equal to the uniform spatial average of P_z(J_1∈D) is invalid, and the subsequent product estimate (4.1) does not follow.

Condition 4.1 as printed contains only one item, namely symmetry of j. Yet Remark 4.2 refers to "condition (2) in (4.1)," and Lemma 4.4 invokes Lemma 4.3, which requires finite variance and an integrability condition on a power of the characteristic function. Neither requirement is stated in Condition 4.1. Symmetric jump densities can have infinite variance or fail the Fourier integrability condition, so the local CLT and all arguments depending on it are unsupported under the theorem's stated assumptions.

The multivariate normalization is mathematically incorrect as stated. The paper writes Var(J_1)=σ^2 and normalizes S_n by σ√n to obtain the standard d-dimensional Gaussian. For a general d-dimensional symmetric random vector the covariance is a matrix, not a scalar; scalar normalization yields a standard Gaussian only under an unstated isotropy condition Cov(J_1)=σ^2I. A symmetric density need not have isotropic covariance.

predicted_errors.error_location: Condition 4.1 discussion immediately after its statement
predicted_errors.supporting_evidence: The claim that p(t,x):=Σ_{n=0}∞e^{-rt}(rt)^n j^{⊗n}(x)/n! is a probability density of X_t is false for a compound Poisson process. X_t has an atom of mass e^{-rt} at zero from the event N_t=0. The n=0 term is a Dirac mass, not a Lebesgue density j^{⊗0}(x).

The sign convention is internally inconsistent. The text says the generator L is non-positive definite and gives semigroup eigenvalues e^{-tλ_n}, but then states Lφ_n=λ_nφ_n. Differentiating P_tφ_n=e^{-tλ_n}φ_n at zero gives Lφ_n=-λ_nφ_n. The displayed eigenvalue equation has the wrong sign.

predicted_errors.error_location: Section 3 claims concerning transition densities, discrete spectra, and (3.1)
predicted_errors.supporting_evidence: A compound Poisson transition law includes a no-jump Dirac component, so it does not admit the asserted ordinary transition density p_D^X(t,x,y) on D without separately retaining a singular identity component. Correspondingly, the killed semigroup contains e^{-rt}I; on L^2 of a continuum domain it is generally not compact and does not have the purely discrete spectral expansion assumed in (3.1). The paper nevertheless uses this expansion as the mechanism for extracting λ_1. This is incompatible with the compound-Poisson setting except under additional, highly nonstandard qualifications.

predicted_errors.error_location: Equation (3.2) and the accompanying statement that it follows from (3.1)
predicted_errors.supporting_evidence: Even given a spectral expansion, −lim_{t→∞}t^{-1}log Q_D^Y(t) equals the lowest eigenvalue only if the coefficient of the lowest eigenspace in Q_D^Y is nonzero. Formula (3.1) has coefficients (∫_Dφ_n)^2, which may vanish. No positivity/irreducibility or nonzero-ground-state-integral condition is stated, so the unconditional assertion of (3.2) is not justified.

The theorem is incomplete: after both statements "If |A|<2^d|D|, then the followings are equivalent:" and "if |A|≥2^d|D|, then the followings are equivalent:" no conditions are listed. It also switches from A to an undefined calligraphic A in its final assertions. Thus the stated theorem has no determinate mathematical content as printed.

The proposition assumes |A|<2^d|E| although E is not defined in the hypotheses; its conclusion then uses E as a centered ellipsoid. In the proof, the assumed equality is changed from Q_D^X(t)=Q_{D^*}^{X^*}(t) to Q_E^X(t)=Q_{E^*}^{X^*}(t). These are not harmless notation changes because E and D play distinct roles, leaving the proposition's hypothesis and proof mismatched.

The transformed density is incorrectly defined as "tilde j=T∘j." If \tilde J=TJ, its density is \tilde j(z)=|det T|^{-1}j(T^{-1}z) (and, under |det T|=1, j(T^{-1}z)), not T∘j. The stated definition does not in general define the distribution of the linearly transformed jumps, so the claimed invariance argument is not correctly formulated.

The proof begins "Without loss of generality, we may assume x=0 and 0∈D" and proves a survival calculation only from 0, but Q_D^X integrates over all starting points x∈D. It then uses ∫_D A(x,n,E)dx, with E undefined. Although a corrected proof could establish a constant conditional retention probability for every current location in D under D-D⊂A, that required argument is absent; the displayed proof does not justify the claimed heat-content formula.

predicted_errors.error_location: Abstract, introduction, and discussion preceding Theorem 2.3
predicted_errors.supporting_evidence: The paper repeatedly states that uniqueness "fails if the jump density is not strictly decreasing," which reads as a general necessity claim. The subsequent construction only considers a particular class of jump laws uniform on specially chosen sets A. It does not prove that every non-strictly-decreasing density has nonunique minimizers. At most it provides a counterexample showing strict decrease cannot be omitted from a universal uniqueness theorem.

The supplied full text cites eleven numbered references, including precise claims such as "[1, Corollary 5.5]" and "[3, Theorem 1]," but contains no bibliography or reference list. Consequently the cited claims, theorem versions, and attributions cannot be verified, and the paper does not meet the minimum requirement for checkable scholarly citations.
